cohort: The study participants included children with presumed (n=43, born >=36 gestational weeks) or neonatal (n=86, born <36 gestational weeks) periventricular venous infarction and a matched control group (n=2168, >=36 gestational weeks).
finding: Maternal bacterial infections, particularly pyelonephritis between gestational weeks 21 and 31, are associated with an increased risk for developing periventricular venous infarction.
gest_age: >=36 gestational weeks (presumed cases and controls), <36 gestational weeks (neonatal cases)
